Inhaled/nasal route - not affected by food

summary: Ipratropium bromide is an inhaled short-acting muscarinic antagonist (SAMA) used as a bronchodilator in COPD and as adjunct in acute asthma, and intranasally for rhinorrhea. By blocking acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in airway smooth muscle it reduces bronchoconstriction and secretions. It has minimal systemic absorption, a slower onset than beta-2 agonists, and is often combined with albuterol/salbutamol. Care is needed to avoid eye contact with the aerosol and in narrow-angle glaucoma or bladder outlet obstruction.
indications: Maintenance bronchodilator treatment of bronchospasm associated with COPD (chronic bronchitis and emphysema)
Adjunctive treatment of acute bronchospasm (e.g., acute asthma exacerbation, with a beta-2 agonist)
Symptomatic relief of rhinorrhea associated with allergic and non-allergic perennial rhinitis or the common cold (nasal spray)

dosage.d: 500 mcg nebulized with a beta-2 agonist
dosage.n: In emergency settings every 20 min x3 then as needed

admin: Shake metered-dose inhaler before use; prime if new or unused for a while
Avoid spraying into the eyes - can cause blurred vision or worsen glaucoma
For nebulization, use a mouthpiece where possible and a nebulizer device
Rinse mouth after inhalation to reduce dry mouth/taste effects
Slower onset than salbutamol - not the first-line reliever for sudden severe attacks alone
moa: Ipratropium is a quaternary anticholinergic (muscarinic receptor antagonist) that competitively blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors on bronchial smooth muscle. This prevents the increase in intracellular cyclic GMP that mediates vagally-induced bronchoconstriction, producing bronchodilation. Its quaternary structure limits systemic absorption and central effects. Intranasally it reduces watery hypersecretion from nasal mucosal glands.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to ipratropium, atropine or its derivatives
Known allergy to soya lecithin / related food products (certain MDI formulations)
monitor: Eye symptoms (pain, blurred vision, halos) suggesting acute glaucoma
Bronchodilator response and any paradoxical bronchospasm

preg: Ipratropium is poorly absorbed systemically. Available data have not shown an increased risk of malformations; it is generally considered acceptable in pregnancy when bronchodilation is needed, but use only if clearly indicated.
lact: Ipratropium is a quaternary amine that is poorly excreted into milk and poorly absorbed orally by the infant. It is considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required; systemic absorption from the inhaled/nasal route is minimal.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required because of minimal systemic absorption.

moderate: Other anticholinergic drugs (additive antimuscarinic effects - dry mouth, urinary retention, glaucoma risk)
Tiotropium or other long-acting antimuscarinics (avoid duplication)
minor: Beta-2 agonists (additive bronchodilation - usually beneficial and intended)

serious: Acute narrow-angle glaucoma (especially if sprayed into eyes)

monitoring: Urinary symptoms in older men or those with prostatism
Watch for paradoxical bronchospasm after dosing
counsel: Use a spacer and avoid getting the spray in your eyes
This is a maintenance/adjunct bronchodilator - keep a fast-acting reliever for sudden attacks unless told otherwise
Rinse your mouth after use to reduce dry mouth and bad taste
Report eye pain, blurred vision, halos around lights, or difficulty passing urine
Stop and seek help if breathing worsens immediately after a dose (paradoxical bronchospasm)
pk: Store at 15-30 C; protect MDI from freezing; protect nebulizer vials from light
pearls: Short-acting muscarinic antagonist (SAMA) - slower onset than beta-2 agonists
Frequently combined with salbutamol/albuterol for additive bronchodilation
Quaternary structure means minimal systemic absorption and few central effects
Keep the aerosol away from the eyes to avoid precipitating glaucoma
Useful add-on in acute severe asthma and COPD exacerbations
missed: Use the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed one and continue your normal routine - do not double the dose.
overdose: Because of low systemic absorption, overdose by inhalation is unlikely to cause serious anticholinergic effects, though dry mouth or visual accommodation difficulties may occur. Management is supportive and symptomatic; effects are usually transient.
